newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aborigines to lodge land claim for Australian city.
newsitem.headline: Aborigines to lodge land claim for Australian city.

text.p: Aborigines plan to lodge a land claim covering the city of Darwin in the Northern Territory -- the first land claim to cover an Australian capital city, the powerful aboriginal Northern Land Council said on Monday.
The Larrakia aboriginal people will on Wednesday lodge their native title land claim which covers undeveloped government land including beaches, parks, mangroves, creeks and nature reserves.
The Larrakia will also seek government compensation for past and future development of their traditional lands on which Darwin is built.
A land council spokesman told Reuters that under native title land laws Aborigines could only seek compensation for post-1994 development of traditional lands.
Darwin, with a population of about 70,000, is Australia's most northern city and sits on the coast of the Arafura Sea which separates Australia from Indonesia.
The land council said in a statement that the Larrakia people, an estimated few thousand, wanted "co-existence" with the people of Darwin.
"While we want our native title rights respected, we do not want to prevent the public from using beaches and enjoying our natural heritage," a Larrakia spokesman said in the statement.
"We want the people of Darwin to continue to enjoy their recreation activities while protecting our sacred sites and the environment, the spokesman said.

The Northern Land Council said it backed the land claim, but stressed it did not cover homes, businesses, schools, hospitals, roads or public works. Land council chairman Galarrwuy Yunupingu said the Larrakia were not opposed to development.

"It is wrong to say native title stops development," Yunupingu said. "The Larrakia want to negotiate appropriate compensation arrangements with developers, this has nothing to do with a so-called grab for taxpayers dollars."
However, the Northern Territory government said it would fight the land claim, labelling it a "greedy money grab".
"This will only cause division. It will be resisted, it will be fought," said Northern Territory chief minister Shane Stone.
In 1992 Australia's High Court overturned the historical idea of Terra Nullus, that Australia was an empty land when white settlers arrived in 1788, recognising traditional land rights of Aborigines.

In 1993, the Australian government passed new "Native Title" laws allowing Aborigines to claim land if they could prove uninterrupted traditional usage of the land. This condition has prevented claims against urban Australia and pastoral land.

But Darwin is a young city sprawling from the coast towards the desert outback of the Northern Territory and has much undeveloped land where Aborigines have lived for centuries. There are some 300,000 Aborigines in Australia, the majority of whom live in non-urban areas.
